article.title: Thresholds Are Business Decisions, Not Just Model Settings
article.why: Practical analytical English for data-driven decisions.

paragraphs.en: A classification model often produces a score or probability, but a business action requires a cutoff. Customers above a threshold may receive an offer, transactions may be reviewed, or applications may require additional checks. Many examples use 0.5 as if it were a natural boundary. In practice, 0.5 has no universal business meaning. The appropriate threshold depends on the consequences of false positives and false negatives, the base rate, operational capacity, and the value of the intervention. Consider fraud review. A false negative can allow a costly fraudulent transaction, while a false positive consumes analyst time and may inconvenience a legitimate customer. If the review team can inspect only 5,000 transactions each day, the threshold must also produce a manageable workload. In marketing, contact may be cheap, but excessive messages can create fatigue or unsubscribe risk. The threshold should therefore be connected to expected value rather than selected only from a generic accuracy metric. Precision and recall help describe trade-offs. Lowering a threshold often increases recall while reducing precision. A confusion matrix can translate this into counts, but the organization still needs to assign business meaning to those counts. Calibration matters if predicted probabilities enter an expected-value calculation. A model can rank cases well while probabilities are systematically too high or too low. Base-rate changes can also alter precision and workload even when ranking quality is stable. Threshold selection should be tested on data that reflects the production population and reviewed when costs, capacity, or prevalence change. Scenario analysis is useful: show expected positives captured, false positives, workload, cost, and value across several candidate cutoffs. Decision makers can then see the trade-off instead of receiving a single mysterious number. Fairness, compliance, and customer-experience constraints may rule out thresholds that look financially attractive. The threshold should be versioned as part of the decision policy, with its assumptions documented. Machine learning estimates something about the world; the threshold determines what the organization does with that estimate. Treating the cutoff as a business decision makes model deployment more transparent and easier to govern. Analysts should define the population, observation window, decision rule, and operational constraint before interpreting the metric. paragraphs.zh: 繁中完整翻譯與解說：本文強調分析結果必須放回正確的 baseline、母體、segment、decision cost 與資料生成機制中理解。百分比、總體 KPI、model threshold 或部署後的新資料，都可能因分母、selection、population mix 或舊 policy 而改變含義。
paragraphs.ja: 日本語完全訳・解説：分析結果はbaseline、母集団、segment、decision cost、data generating mechanismと結び付けて解釈する必要がある。percentage、集計KPI、model threshold、deployment後のdataは、分母、selection、population mix、過去policyによって意味が変わり得る。
